original_value: AbstractOften because of limitations in generation capacity of power stations, many developing countries frequently resort to disconnecting large parts of the power grid from supply, a process termed load shedding. This leaves households in disconnected parts without electricity, causing them inconvenience and discomfort. Without fairness being taken into due consideration during load shedding, some households may suffer more than others. In this paper, we solve the fair load shedding problem (FLSP) by creating solutions which connect households to supply based on some fairness criteria (i.e., to fairly connect homes to supply in terms of duration, their electricity needs, and their demand), which we model as their utilities. First, we briefly describe some state-of-art household-level load shedding heuristics which meet the first criteria. Second, we model the FLSP as a resource allocation problem, which we formulate into two Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) problems based on the Multiple Knapsack Problem. In so doing, we use the utilitarian, egalitarian and envy-freeness social welfare metrics to develop objectives and constraints that ensure our FLSP solutions results in fair allocations that consider the utilities of agents. Then, we solve the FLSP and show that our MIP models maximize the groupwise and individual utilities of agents, and minimize the differences between their pairwise utilities under a number of experiments. When taken together, our endeavour establishes a set of benchmarks for fair load shedding schemes, and provide insights for designing fair allocation solutions for other scarce resources.

result.paraphrase: AbstractBecause power stations often have limited generation capacity, many developing countries frequently resort to disconnecting large sections of the power grid from supply, a practice known as load shedding. This leaves households in disconnected areas without electricity, causing inconvenience and discomfort. If fairness is not properly considered during load shedding, some households may be affected more severely than others. In this paper, we address the fair load shedding problem (FLSP) by developing solutions that reconnect households to supply according to fairness criteria—namely, fairly restoring power in terms of duration, electricity needs, and demand, which we model as utilities. First, we briefly review several state-of-the-art household-level load shedding heuristics that satisfy the first criteria. Second, we formulate the FLSP as a resource allocation problem and express it as two Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) problems based on the Multiple Knapsack Problem. In doing so, we use utilitarian, egalitarian, and envy-freeness social welfare metrics to define objectives and constraints that ensure our FLSP solutions produce fair allocations that account for agent utilities. We then solve the FLSP and show through multiple experiments that our MIP models maximize both group and individual utilities, while minimizing differences among pairwise utilities. Overall, our work establishes benchmarks for fair load shedding schemes and offers insights for designing fair allocation solutions for other scarce resources.
